$comment: Every endpoint of this module that answers without an organization permission or the operator check (public or signed-in only; adapter_endpoints: registered on the HTTP server outside /api), and every request Ever Platform makes to an installation through it. routes-manifest.spec.ts compares it with the registered routes; UPDATE_ROUTES_MANIFEST=1 rewrites the method and path list.

public_endpoints.purpose: The paired Ever Teams web app asks it, with the signed-in person's token, whether this installation is connected to Ever Platform.

public_endpoints.mounted_when: EVER_CONNECT_PROVISION_ENABLED=true on a connected installation with the Ever ID sign-in plugin loaded (404 otherwise); 10 requests a minute per address
public_endpoints.answers: {ok, org_display_name, handle, product_tenant_exists, sign_in_required, provision_key}, or 401 intent_invalid / 422 product_mismatch / 409 intent_replayed
public_endpoints.purpose: Verifies Ever Platform's signed request ({intent}) against the root-verified keys and keeps it, by its id, under a new one-time key (only its SHA-256 is stored).

public_endpoints.mounted_when: EVER_CONNECT_PROVISION_ENABLED=true on a connected installation with the Ever ID sign-in plugin loaded (404 otherwise); 10 requests a minute per address
public_endpoints.answers: what the confirmation page shows (the organization's public names, the e-mail of the person's own Ever ID sign-in, what will be created, the return address)

public_endpoints.mounted_when: EVER_CONNECT_PROVISION_ENABLED=true on a connected installation with the Ever ID sign-in plugin loaded (404 otherwise); 10 requests a minute per address
public_endpoints.answers: a static HTML page (Cache-Control: no-store, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, a Content-Security-Policy that allows only its own script and style)
public_endpoints.purpose: Where Ever sends a person to create a workspace, with the signed request in the URL fragment (#intent=<JWS>), which never reaches a server. The page removes it from the address bar, sends it to preflight and opens Sign in with Ever ID with the one-time key it gets.

public_endpoints.mounted_when: EVER_CONNECT_PROVISION_ENABLED=true on a connected installation with the Ever ID sign-in plugin loaded (404 otherwise); 10 requests a minute per address
public_endpoints.answers: 201 {status: created, product_tenant_id, product_org_id, product_user_id, employee_id?, team_id?, sign_in_url, return_to}, 200 {status: exists, ...}, or an application/problem+json error
public_endpoints.purpose: The person confirmed creating the workspace Ever asked for: {provision_key, handoff_key, request: {first_name?, last_name?}}. Both keys are one-time keys (the request kept by preflight, the person's own Ever ID sign-in); the signed-in Ever ID must be the person the request names.

adapter_endpoints.mounted_when: the module is loaded (EVER_CONNECT_ENABLED=true); outside the /api prefix
adapter_endpoints.answers: {"statement": "<compact JWS signed with the connection key>"} while Ever Platform checks the installation's address (at most 10 minutes); otherwise the same 404 as an address that does not exist
adapter_endpoints.purpose: Lets Ever Platform check that this installation answers at the address it was given, after the instance_url integration was consented and accepted.

platform_requests.purpose: Not in this release. Will answer Ever Platform's count of employees and users of a linked organization, only while the usage reporting integration is enabled for it.
